intro: Covers the US session of Thursday 19 November. Published after a delay so the US close could be captured; the SPI futures figure is a range and its level is not verified for this session (see footnotes).
footnotes: US index and VIX figures are from Yahoo Finance quote pages (market closed), consistent with Wednesday's closes (S&P 7,323.63, Nasdaq 24,429.89, Dow 50,198.17) and Yahoo's live report of a roughly 2% fall with the Dow down over 1,100 points.
The 10-year change is versus the 5.07% close reported by FNArena (Yahoo shows -1 bp, Trading Economics -3 bp).

Brent, gold, AUD/USD and iron ore are Trading Economics CFD reference prices dated 19 Nov; Yahoo's Brent futures quote (US$90.08) differs and is not used. Spot gold fell 1.75% (gold futures about -2.2%).

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures point sharply lower: Motley Fool Australia's pre-open note has the ASX 200 set to open 105 points or 1.2% lower, while Investing.com shows the December contract down 1.5% (8,655 vs 8,787.5). A TradingView figure of -0.5% looks stale and is disregarded. Taking the midpoint of 1.2-1.5%, the implied ASX 200 open is roughly -118 points or -1.35%, around 8,612 (range about 8,600-8,625). The ASX 200 closed Thursday at 8,730.40, down 91.4 points or 1.04%, a 20-day low. The futures level itself is not verified for this session.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data release or RBA event identified in this run; check FNArena's financial calendar for 20 November.
Economists are flagging recession risk after recent local data.
what_moved: A broad risk-off session: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each lost about 2% and the Dow more than 1,100 points, extending a losing run (the S&P 500 was heading for a sixth straight loss) as the Anthropic IPO debut drew attention away from the rest of the market and rate-hike worries kept pressure on equities and metals. Per Yahoo Finance's sector heatmap, Energy (+1.29%) and Utilities (+0.44%) led; Consumer Cyclical (-2.84%), Communication Services (-2.82%), Industrials (-2.20%) and Technology (-2.00%) lagged. The VIX jumped about 18% to near 29.

news.headline: Wall Street sells off as Anthropic debuts
news.summary: Anthropic shares rose sharply in the largest US listing debut on record while the broader market fell; reports differ on the closing gain (about 17% to 27%).

news.headline: Weak US labour and survey data
news.summary: Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 (consensus 197,000), continuing claims rose 70,000 to 1.763 million, and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell to 6.3 from 20.9.

news.headline: Gold at a 14-month low
news.summary: Gold slid on a stronger US dollar and rising rate-hike bets.

news.headline: ASX 200 falls to a 20-day low
news.summary: The index lost 1.04% to 8,730.40 as miners and gold stocks sold off; economists warn the data shows Australia approaching recession.

news.headline: Fed hike talk and metals rout (Wednesday session)
news.summary: Fed Governor Waller argued a 50bp hike in December was possible if the FOMC does not signal another hike in January; copper fell to its lowest since April and a BofA survey showed net tech overweight falling to 12% from 37%.

coming_up: The next FOMC decision (December; exact date not verified in this run) is the key event, with Fed commentary on further hikes in focus. Weekly US jobless claims are due next Thursday.
